title: MERGE Statement (PostgreSQL 15+)
description: Execute conditional INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations in a single SQL standard MERGE statement.

data.text: Introduced in PostgreSQL 15, the **`MERGE`** statement provides standard ANSI SQL compliance for reconciling two datasets. It allows you to specify `WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE / DELETE` and `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT` in a single unified command.

data.title: Reconciling Warehouse Staging Data with MERGE
data.content: Synchronizing staging customer data into production tables.
data.code:
MERGE INTO customers AS target
USING staging_customers AS source
ON target.email = source.email
WHEN MATCHED AND source.is_deleted = true THEN
    DELETE
WHEN MATCHED THEN
    UPDATE SET 
        name = source.name,
        updated_at = NOW()
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT (email, name, created_at)
    VALUES (source.email, source.name, NOW());

data.text: A Full MERGE with All Three Branches

A MERGE clause list is evaluated in order, and the first matching clause wins. This makes the order of `WHEN MATCHED` conditions important: a soft-delete flag checked before an update prevents updating a row that should be removed.

data.title: Upsert and delete in one statement
data.content: Existing rows are updated only when the source is newer, rows flagged for deletion are removed, and new rows are inserted.
data.code:
MERGE INTO customers AS c
USING staging_customers AS s
    ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.is_deleted THEN
    DELETE
WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at > c.updated_at THEN
    UPDATE SET
        name       = s.name,
        email      = s.email,
        updated_at = s.updated_at
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT (customer_id, name, email, updated_at)
    VALUES (s.customer_id, s.name, s.email, s.updated_at);

data.title: MERGE is not concurrency-safe by itself
data.text: MERGE reads and then modifies, so concurrent transactions can still conflict in ways the statement cannot resolve for you. For a simple upsert on a unique key, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` is usually safer and shorter. MERGE earns its place when you need conditional DELETE or a mixture of branches that ON CONFLICT cannot express. Note that PostgreSQL's MERGE has no RETURNING clause.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `MERGE` was added in PostgreSQL 15 as an ANSI SQL standard alternative to `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`.
Supports conditional `DELETE` when rows match specific criteria.
Widely used in ETL pipelines and data warehousing reconciliations.
